request: How does a transformer turn scores into a guess for the next word?

composition.story: For “The cat sat on the …”, inspect scores for three word-sized tokens: mat, rug, moon. Advance to probabilities, then the highest-probability guess. This toy uses only these tokens, fixed scores, temperature one, and greedy decoding.

aha.observation: Softmax converts scores into probabilities; greedy decoding chooses the most probable token, not a certain answer.

parts.presentation: Place below the story and instructions. Show the active step and completed trace here only.
Show one candidate row with fixed token positions. Region phases follow variant.states order. Highlight the active region without animation.
Anchor beside the candidate row without covering it. Identify the mechanism without repeating numerical values.
Keep token readouts in picture order. Scores are unitless; probabilities cover the same toy vocabulary and round to one decimal percent.

controls.label: Process step
controls.presentation: Previous and Next; default Scores; increment one state. Keep boundary names when disabled. Every state persists until action. Provide keyboard operation and visible focus.

controls.label: Reset
controls.presentation: Restore Scores and all defaults. Parameter-control budget: zero, excluding navigation and reset. Support Enter and Space with visible focus.

regions.label: Next-token candidates
phases: Scores: mat leads; rug follows; moon trails.
Probabilities: mat has the largest share; rug and moon remain possible.

states.label: Scores
states.sentence: The candidate row starts with the transformer's scores.
states.why: Scores rank candidates, but they are not probabilities.

states.label: Probabilities
states.sentence: Softmax turns the candidate scores into probability shares.
states.why: Exponentiate each score, then divide by their sum; the largest score keeps the largest share.

states.label: Guess
states.sentence: The candidate row marks mat as the greedy next-token guess.
states.why: Greedy decoding chooses the largest probability; the remaining probability shows why that choice is not certain.
